summary: llm-consortium is a plugin for Simon Willison's `llm` CLI, not a standalone agent. It adds a `llm consortium` command group and registers each saved consortium as an `llm` model. When you prompt one (`llm -m <name> "prompt"`), it sends the prompt to several member models in parallel through `llm.get_model(...)`. An arbiter model then combines the answers into one, and the cycle repeats until a confidence threshold or the iteration limit is reached. All model traffic goes through llm's built-in OpenAI chat client, which uses the openai Python SDK. The recipe sets up one OpenAI-compatible model, `proxy-model`, in llm's `extra-openai-models.yaml` with api_base=$PROXY_URL/v1. It saves a consortium of 2 instances of that model, with the same model as arbiter. It then runs the task text once through `llm -m cns "$TASK"`. The result is text only: this harness has no tools and cannot read or edit files in the working directory.
dockerfile:
ARG BASE=python:3.12-slim-bookworm
FROM ${BASE}
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
RUN (command -v curl >/dev/null && [ -f /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt ]) || \
    (apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*)
ENV UV_INSTALL_DIR=/opt/harness/uv \
    UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=/opt/harness/python \
    UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/uv-cache \
    UV_NO_CONFIG=1
RUN mkdir -p /opt/harness/bin && curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | env INSTALLER_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1 sh
COPY . /opt/harness/src
RUN cd /opt/harness/src \
 && /opt/harness/uv/uv python install 3.12 \
 && /opt/harness/uv/uv venv --python 3.12 /opt/harness/venv \
 && /opt/harness/uv/uv export --frozen --no-dev --no-emit-project --no-hashes -o /tmp/req.txt \
 && /opt/harness/uv/uv pip install --python /opt/harness/venv/bin/python -r /tmp/req.txt -e /opt/harness/src \
 && ln -s /opt/harness/venv/bin/llm /opt/harness/bin/llm \
 && rm -rf /tmp/uv-cache /tmp/req.txt
ENV PATH=/opt/harness/bin:$PATH \
    LLM_CONSORTIUM_SKIP_DEP_CHECK=1
RUN echo 'case ":$PATH:" in *:/opt/harness/bin:*) ;; *) export PATH=/opt/harness/bin:$PATH ;; esac' > /etc/profile.d/00-harness.sh
run_command:
set -e
mkdir -p /out
D="$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/io.datasette.llm"; mkdir -p "$D"
printf -- '- model_id: proxy-model\n  model_name: gpt-4o\n  api_base: "%s/v1"\n  can_stream: true\n' "$PROXY_URL" > "$D/extra-openai-models.yaml"
llm consortium save cns -m proxy-model:2 --arbiter proxy-model --min-iterations 1 --max-iterations 2 --confidence-threshold 0.8 >/dev/null
llm -m cns "$TASK" | tee /out/answer.md
check_command: llm --version && llm consortium --help >/dev/null && llm plugins | grep -q llm-consortium && echo ok
notes:
Tested locally with Docker against a fake OpenAI-compatible server, on both python:3.12-slim-bookworm and buildpack-deps:jammy. The CLI loads, the plugin registers, and a full consortium run finishes. It makes several chat-completions calls: two members plus the arbiter per iteration, some streaming and some not, plus possible arbiter "repair" retries.
- **Config and logs:** XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/out/config puts everything in /out/config/io.datasette.llm. This is needed because the consortium db ignores LLM_USER_PATH and uses click.get_app_dir. That folder holds llm's own logs.db (every prompt and response), consortium_logs.db (runs, iterations, arbiter decisions) and the model yaml. The final answer is also written to /out/answer.md.
- **Editable install:** the repo's package-data list leaves out arbiter_system.xml and the rank_*.xml prompts. A normal wheel install logs "Error reading arbiter_system.xml", so the Dockerfile uses an editable install from /opt/harness/src.
- **PATH:** a profile.d script adds /opt/harness/bin back to PATH, because Debian's /etc/profile resets PATH in `bash -lc`.
- **Pinned versions:** dependencies come from uv.lock, including llm 0.19.1.
- **Limitation:** this is a prompt-to-answer tool, not a coding agent. It cannot run shell commands or edit files in the task directory, so benchmark tasks that need file changes will fail.
